newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy rejects rumours of car scrapping incentives.
newsitem.headline: Italy rejects rumours of car scrapping incentives.

text.p: The Italian government has no plans to introduce incentives in the forthcoming budget to encourage people to scrap their old cars and buy new ones, the Finance Ministry said in a statement on Friday.

Rumours have been circulating in the press recently that the government was thinking about introducing schemes similar to those already seen in France and Spain which were aimed at boosting new car sales.
The Italian car market has been depressed for much of 1996 and Italy's car and industrial giant Fiat on Wednesday reported its first half 1996 profits fell 28 percent.
It warned that underlying profits for the whole of 1996 would fall short of 1995, fuelling rumours that the government might step in and seek to lift the domestic car market.

"Regarding talk that possible incentives to scrap used cars will be included in the forthcoming budget package, the finance and industry ministries categorically deny that this is being studied," the Finance Ministry's brief statement said.
The government is expected to unveil its 1997 budget before the end of the month. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
